details: The US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, rose to 4.1% year-over-year in May, surpassing expectations and remaining well above the Fed's 2% target. This higher-than-anticipated inflation data is strengthening market expectations for the Federal Reserve to maintain a hawkish monetary policy, potentially leading to further interest rate hikes or delaying any cuts. The news triggered a "risk-off" sentiment in financial markets, causing Bitcoin to briefly dip below $58,000 and leading to significant liquidations across the broader cryptocurrency market.
title: US May PCE Inflation Surges, Fuels Fed Rate Hike Fears

details: The US Senate has passed the "21st Century ROAD to Housing Act," which includes a provision to temporarily ban the Federal Reserve from issuing or creating a central bank digital currency (CBDC) until December 31, 2030. This legislative move, which is anticipated to be signed into law, is generally viewed as a positive development for decentralized cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin. By removing the immediate threat of a government-issued digital dollar, the ban is expected to alleviate concerns about competition and potentially bolster the appeal and adoption of existing cryptocurrencies.
title: US Senate Blocks Fed CBDC Until 2030, Boosts Decentralized Crypto
